requirements.text: put together a knowledge article called 'SAP Oracle Database Memory Leak Resolution' ... Here is the article content
requirements.selector: title = 'SAP Oracle Database Memory Leak Resolution'
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge WHERE title = 'SAP Oracle Database Memory Leak Resolution' AND state = 'published' AND visibility = 'internal' AND owner_id = 'USER_004' AND org_id = 'ORG_001' AND body LIKE '%24789456%' AND body LIKE '%Root Cause Analysis%' AND body LIKE '%Resolution Steps%' AND body LIKE '%Prevention Measures%'
assumptions: two knowledge articles are created, so this one is selected by its title, not anchored by an assumed id (KB_026 or KB_027)
state published kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the request says 'put together', not publish)
visibility internal kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the request asks for external users only for the FAQ)
owner_id USER_004: the acting user (active manager, ORG_001), named as author in the supplied content
org_id ORG_001: the acting user's organisation and the parent incident's

the body must hold the supplied content (what went wrong, how it was fixed); tested by the Oracle patch number and three section headings it contains, since an exact match would depend on whitespace and quoting; no benchmark check tests the body

disagreement: body: A LIKE '%24789456%', B LIKE the three headings 'Root Cause Analysis', 'Resolution Steps', 'Prevention Measures'; chose all four predicates because every token is in the supplied content, so both are right and together they are tighter
disagreement: cells: A repeats the selector's title as a cell, B does not; dropped it because the selector already fixes the title with the same condition

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on all six benchmark checks (kept), the two created articles selected by title, the four resolution links selected by natural key, the boundary stay on other incidents, and KB_020 published with external visibility. disagreement: KB_020's external visibility: one pass has it as a requirement of its own carrying 'Verify Windows 11 FAQ Has External Visibility', the other carries that check jointly on the publish requirement; dropped the separate requirement because it tests a subset of the same row's cells, so the joint requirement is tighter and the check stays carried. disagreement: body cells of both created articles: the passes test different tokens of the supplied content; kept the union (logged in each requirement). disagreement: cells of the three knowledge requirements: one pass repeats the selector's title as a cell; dropped (logged in each requirement). disagreement: form of the four link selectors and the boundary stay: one pass describes the article in words; chose the subquery on the title (logged in the requirements). disagreement: form of the FAQ-mention cell: one pass parenthesises the disjunction; chose the bare disjunction, which the sql parenthesises (logged in the requirement). disagreement: texts: one pass adds parentheticals naming each child incident; kept the request's own words. Acting user USER_004 (Joanne Simpson) is an active manager in ORG_001 with full CRUD on knowledge. The incident_knowledge links carry an org_id; the seed's links take the incident's organisation, and neither the request nor the policy fixes it, so it is not tested. INC_044 (ORG_007) and INC_082 (ORG_016) lie outside the acting user's organisation; the request says 'if possible', but the policy gives a manager CRUD on knowledge and incidents with no organisation limit, so all four links are required, as the benchmark expects. The pattern '%KB_020%' treats the underscore as a single-character wildcard, so it also accepts 'KB-020' or 'KB 020'; kept as the benchmark wrote it. The body tokens are the only cells no benchmark check tests.
